final.summary: The ETP stopped during the treatment interval and inflow and outfall flows were zero while it was stopped, with power confirmed by photo. Outfall pH stayed near neutral and balances were within tolerance, showing no bypass signal. The equalization tank level is missing over the stop, so it cannot be shown that arriving wastewater was held in the tank.

key_evidence.why: Power at standby level through the claimed stop window, showing the ETP was stopped.
ETP inflow zero through the stop, showing no flow was passing the ETP inlet.
Outfall flow zero through the stop, showing nothing passed the outfall meter.
Photo reading matches the feed and sits at expected standby power, proving the stop was real.
Outfall pH stayed near neutral with no excursion above 9, showing no raw wastewater reached the outfall.
ETP and boundary balances within tolerance, showing no missing bypass volume over the interval.
Power matched the expected band for its inflow over the interval, showing aeration ran when the plant was on.
Power feed shows no identical repeat of another day, ruling out a replayed feed.

final.scope_line: Based on flow, power, pH and conductivity records for 2026-10-13 10:00 to 2026-10-14 14:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: Equalization tank level T1 has no coverage over the treatment interval, so the tank balance cannot be computed and the rise of stored water cannot be checked.
S2 and S4a show flat zero stretches during the stop; a stuck meter cannot be fully ruled out on its own, though separate signals agree.
Lab sample at 13:20 was taken while the ETP was stopped and outfall flow was zero, so it does not represent treated effluent from the batch.
Conductivity over the full interval was not retrieved within the check budget, so a conductivity check for dilution was not completed.
Factory logbook and maintenance record are claims, not facts; the maintenance record work order number differs from the logbook reference.

evidence_request.reason: A rising tank level with ETP at standby and zero outfall flow would show arriving wastewater was held, separating a held stop from overflow or bypass.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
